title: Monitoring Bat Fauna in Forests Using Mist Nets
author: Alona Prylutska
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6q5hdy6

steps.title: Determine Capture Period
steps.instruction: Select the timing for bat captures, ideally in July when young individuals begin to fly and before autumn migration starts.

steps.title: Select Study Plot and Capture Points
steps.instruction: Identify a study plot of approximately 400-500 ha containing diverse habitats (e.g., lake, river shores, forest edges, and closed forest roads) and establish 9 capture points.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the distance between capture sites is no less than 600 m and up to 3000 m.

steps.title: Install and Monitor Mist Nets
steps.instruction: Deploy nylon mist nets (12 x 3 m, mesh size 15 mm) and monitor them throughout the night.

substeps.instruction: Install the net from sunset until 10–30 min before sunrise.
Remain near the net all night to prevent bats from escaping.
Keep captured bats in textile bags near the net throughout the night.

steps.title: Execute Mist-Netting Rounds
steps.instruction: Perform two rounds of mist-netting at each of the 9 capture sites for a total of 18 capture nights.

substeps.instruction: Complete the first round of 9 capture nights (one at each point).
Complete the second round of 9 capture nights (one at each point).

steps.title: Process and Release Bats
steps.instruction: Perform biometrical processing and record specific data for each individual before releasing them.

substeps.instruction: Record species, sex, age, and identified breeding status of adult individuals of both sexes.
Release all animals as soon as possible during dark time.
